name: San Ramon
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in San Ramon, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in San Ramon, CA: Glow in the Meadow lights, a Bishop Ranch ice rink, Forest Home Farms tours and free holiday concerts.
lede: San Ramon pairs city light shows and concerts with a historic farm and a Bishop Ranch ice rink, so a December week can mix glowing lights, skating and an old fashioned Victorian Christmas.
celebrates: The City of San Ramon runs much of the season through its Parks and Community Services department. Central Park Meadow becomes a lit winter walk called Glow in the Meadow all December, after a free kick off night. At Forest Home Farms Historic Park, which is on the National Register of Historic Places, the city hosts a free holiday afternoon and Victorian Christmas tours in the Glass House. City Center at Bishop Ranch sets up the Kristi Yamaguchi Holiday Ice Rink with skate rental included, and holiday concerts play at Dougherty Station and the Dougherty Valley Performing Arts Center.
lastyear: We could not find a published recap of San Ramon's 2025 holiday events, so this page relies on the City of San Ramon's own 2026 pages. The city lists its holiday programs together on a seasonal events page: Glow in the Meadow lights in Central Park, holiday performances at Dougherty Station and the Dougherty Valley Performing Arts Center, and special days at Forest Home Farms. Check those pages before you go, since the city updates them through December.
facts: San Ramon takes its name from the Spanish for Saint Raymond, after a Native American vaquero who tended mission sheep on the land. The area became part of the Rancho San Ramon land grant to Jose Maria Amador in 1834, and Leo and Mary Jane Norris, the first permanent American settlers, bought the northwest corner of the rancho in 1850. San Ramon became the official place name when a post office opened in 1873, and the city incorporated on July 1, 1983.
trains: Trains once ran through San Ramon. The Southern Pacific Railroad finished its San Ramon Branch Line in 1891 and extended it south to Radum on February 7, 1909, and passenger service ended in 1934. Contra Costa County later obtained the right of way, and the Iron Horse Regional Trail follows the old route today. The closest BART station is West Dublin/Pleasanton, about 6 miles away, and County Connection buses serve the city.
traditions: Eight light installations in Central Park Meadow all December, with a free kick off night.
A free, registration required afternoon at Forest Home Farms Historic Park.
Glass House tours at Forest Home Farms with timed entry.
An outdoor rink at City Center Bishop Ranch with skate rental included.
A free community chorus concert at Dougherty Station and a symphonic band concert in Dougherty Valley.
kidfact: San Ramon's name comes from Saint Raymond, and the town grew up around a ranch and a farm. You can still visit one of them, Forest Home Farms, today.
faq: Where can kids see Christmas lights in San Ramon?

Glow in the Meadow fills Central Park Meadow at 12501 Alcosta Boulevard with eight light installations throughout December. The city lights the meadow daily for self guided strolling after a free kick off night, so families can pick any evening that suits bedtime.
Is there an ice rink in San Ramon?

Yes. The Kristi Yamaguchi Holiday Ice Rink is at City Center Bishop Ranch, 6000 Bollinger Canyon Road. Skate rental is included with admission, and the rink runs through early January with several daily sessions listed on its ticket page.
Are there free Christmas events in San Ramon?

Yes. The Glow in the Meadow kick off, Holiday on the Farm at Forest Home Farms and the Community Chorus holiday concert at Dougherty Station are all listed as free by the City of San Ramon. Some of them ask families to register ahead.
Can kids see a historic Christmas in San Ramon?

Forest Home Farms Historic Park offers Victorian Christmas tours of the Glass House and a free holiday afternoon. The farm is on the National Register of Historic Places, so children can see how a family farmhouse celebrated long ago.
Is there a train to San Ramon for the holidays?

There is no passenger train in San Ramon today. The old Southern Pacific branch, finished in 1891, is now the Iron Horse Regional Trail, and the closest BART station is West Dublin/Pleasanton, about 6 miles away. County Connection buses serve the city for families without a car.
